lines.english: "Ogiso… why are you…?"
"…! U-Uh, umm… could it be that… you were listening?"
"Listening…?"
I figure she'd get suspicious if someone had sprinted up to the rooftop and was gasping for air for no good reason.
"I-I'm sorry! Please forget what just happened!"
"Forget…?"
Forget that you were singing here? Or that you asked such a pointless question just now?
"Ah, um, well… what I mean is… I just got a little carried away and did something embarrassing."
"W-Well… at first, I was just looking at the schoolyard. You know, at the track team, the tennis team, and the handball team."
"O-Okay…"
"And then, you know… I heard a familiar song from the floor below…"
"Yeah…"
"It made me kind of happy. The truth is, I really love White Album… even if it may be a bit old."
"Me too… it was the first CD I bought with my own allowance."
"Really!? We're a good match then!
…Ahh, that's not what I meant, um…"
"Um, hey…"
"Y-Yes?"
"About the school festival this year…"
"The school festival? Ah, you mean the contest?"
"N-No. It's not that."
"Uh, um…?"
"…I forgot."
"Well, you said, 'forget it' just a moment ago."
"Ah, ah… ah～!"
What am I trying to say here…
"I'll be going then. Sorry for bothering you."
Really, didn't I decide that I'd stop?
"You weren't… bothering me at all."
My shoddy guitar accompanied by perfect piano playing.
"Thanks."
And right at the last minute, a beautiful singer appears. A group as fantastic as this sounds too good to be true, doesn't it?
"Not at all. I should be thanking you."
I should just forget about it. I have to think about Ogiso's circumstances here.
"Then, I'll see you tomorrow."
She hates standing out so much, she even hesitated to participate in the Miss Houjou High contest.
"Yup, goodbye. See you tomorrow."
There's no way she'd do something as flashy as stand on stage and sing in front of everyone, right?
"…! Ah, no!"
"Mr. Executive Committee Member's… helper?"
Even so…
"Listen…"
"Yes?"
"…Would you like to join the Light Music Club? We're performing at the festival, but we don't have a singer."
Why did I just say that? I'm such an idiot…
"You're fine with this being the final draft of the stage program, then? I'll be submitting it during lunch break."
"…Yeah."
Getting the program just before the deadline, Chikashi gives me a light frown, as if to show that he's somewhat aware of the situation.
"Is this really okay? You've got a plan, right?"
"…Who knows?"
"Don't just casually say that! You're making me feel uneasy here!"
I've made no changes to the submitted entries or their order.
"Recently, even Takeya seems to be just about ready to give up… This couldn't be your doing now, could it…?"
"Don't just keep quiet like that! You're making me even more une… what?"
"What's wrong, Chika… eh?"
"The bell… hasn't rung yet, right?"
"Ah… eeh?"
Having stayed up all night, what now reflects in my dreary eyes is the image of the neighboring student. For once, her expression seems to be showing a tiny bit of emotion.
Even more surprising than that is the fact that there's still fifteen minutes until class starts.
"W-What? What's the matter?"
"…Yesterday…"
"Ah, there you are, there you are! Harukiii～!"
Just as she was about to open her mouth on that overly refined face of hers; as if to lambaste me with complaints…
"Haah…"
She glared at me for a moment, then violently took her seat.
We hadn't talked in so long, and it looked like we finally got the chance just now…
"Haruki! Harukiii～! Someone's looking for you! And a really phenomenal person at that!"
"Oh, shut up! You could at least be a little more quiet if you want to make a racket!"
"Don't be unreasonable…"
"Don't be so unreasonable…"
But for the neighboring student to come talk to me… this was like the second time this year she'd done that.
"Besides, you always exaggerate, Io. When did you even learn a word like phenome…"
"U-Um, good morning. Kitahara-kun… was your name, right?"
"Eh?"
"Eh?"
Io always exaggerates, but in a rare case of her actually meaning what she said, she actually did bring someone phenomenal.
"Hey, hang on, what the… what is it? What the hell's going on over there right now?"
"You really do get wind of this sort of thing in an instant…"
"What's with you suddenly barging into someone else's classroom?"
"Aren't you from a different class too, Io…?"
"Shh! Ogiso's saying something! …It seems really awkward."
"Awkward…"
"Oh, man! You should be taking it step by step, Haruki! What are you doing, trying to beat the final boss at the very beginning!?"
"You're one to talk, always doing nothing but grinding."
"Uh, umm…"
"Uh…"
We're still stuck on the conversation from yesterday.
I didn't think she would come all the way here to seriously respond to my crazy invitation.
I even thought she'd refuse me with a smile, a scornful gaze, or maybe a half-tearful look on her face.
"Could you wait a day?"
That was all she said last evening, on the rooftop.
"Um… about yesterday's question… I'm sorry for making you wait."
"No, I should be the one apologizing for suddenly saying something like that. You must've been surprised, I'm sorry."
"N-Not at all! I understand where you were coming from, considering how much of a bind you were in…"
"No, well that's true, but… it's nothing you should feel the need to involve yourself with."
"So anyway… I went home following what happened yesterday, and spent the whole night thinking about it without getting any sleep."
"The… whole night?"
She thought about it that seriously…? Does that mean there's still a glimmer of hope…?
"Here, have a look, my eyes look a bit swollen, right? …Yours seem that way too, don't they, Kitahara-kun?"
"Ah, no, for me, I…"
I simply had so much work to do that I had no time to sleep.
"I was thinking about whether someone like me could do it, whether I could do it the way I am now, and whether I really wanted to do it."
She was really giving this some serious thought…
This must be the first time I've troubled a girl like this ever since I was born.
On top of that… it's a girl who draws so much attention; I've been feeling so many gazes piercing through me for a while now.
"And you see… a little while ago, I finally came to a conclusion."
"Is… that so…?"
"I'm sorry… it was by a narrow margin, but I really can't do it."
"…I see."
But…
This unattainable flower of a girl, ultimately gives me an answer that's befitting of her stature.
"Haruki! You've… really got some balls…"
"Hey, homeroom bell's ringing. Is it really okay for you to be here?"
"How was it? What did Setsuna say to turn you down?"
"…Hold on, what I said just now wasn't directed only at Takeya."
The pair of outsiders greeted me as I returned to the classroom.
"Seriously though, how'd it go? No matter how you look at it…"
"Yeah… indeed, she refused my request."
"I knew it…"
"I knew it…"
"I knew it…"
"But… she said she'd like us to stay friends."
"Ahh, how could this happen?"
"The usual cliche response."
"A clear rejection."
"Was it… really a rejection?"
"Well, you see, Kitahara-kun… I do realize that refusing your request and making one myself is a rather selfish thing to do…"
"Still, I know it'll be hard for me to face you in the future if I don't tell you now, and I don't want that… so I'll ask away, alright?"
"From now on… would it be fine if we kept in touch?"
"That, and also… this is quite brazen of me, but…"
"Would you… like to go to the school festival with me?"
The nuance was kind of… well, no matter.
"…Let's go for karaoke after school, Haruki. We'll party so hard you'll forget all about it, all right?"
"I'm coming too… It'll be our treat today."
"Yeah… even if it's painful or sad, we'll help you forget it all."
"Stop trying to console me. It's gross."
"We get it! We get it already! You don't have to say any more!"
"We'll look the other way when you're crying, so no worries, Haruki."
"I'll lend you my shoulder as well. If it's only for crying anyway…"
"That's disgusting! And I can't go today anyway. There's still something I have to do."
That's right… I can't lose heart over this.
That's because…
Past Minami-Suetsugu Station, the entertainment district for the students; the second closest station to school, Suetsugu-chou Station, shows an unchanging scenery.
The florist turns off the brilliant lights within her store, emphasizing its solitary atmosphere in front of the station.
A girl with braids diligently stocks the shelves of a supermarket's storefront.
An elderly person with a cane leisurely walks up and down the street, clearly without a real destination in mind…
"Ogiso!"
It's a scenery that would never change, no matter when I came.
The diligent, braided girl who does her best to tend to the grocery store front.
"I'd like to discuss it with you one more time… Is that all right?"
"Ah… um…"
I would never lose heart over a single rejection.
That's because…
I know that I still have one last chance.
In the park just behind the station.
Sitting on the rusty, creaking swings, Ogiso and I slowly swing back and forth in silence.

From the homemade-looking shopping bag by Ogiso's feet, I can see a long leek sticking out, as well as Chinese cabbage, shiitake mushrooms, and strings of konnyaku. My body warms up just from imagining her menu for tonight.
Looks like she went to get some leftover food from the grocery store… How thrifty of her.
"I see, I see… So that's what it was…"
"…What was?"
The dissonant noise of creaking metal ceases, and a beautiful voice rings out like the sound of a bell.
"I was a bit taken aback when I first talked to you, Kitahara-kun."
…Though it has the same pitch as the creaking, the way it touches my ears feels completely different.
"Was it something I said?"
"Like, 'she's got her own share of worries,' or, 'she'd be troubled if she became too famous'…"
"Ahh…"
"So you knew about it all along… this side of me."
Ogiso touches her slightly dropped glasses with her fingers, and stares at me with slight resentment.
"No, I'm really sorry. I was planning on taking it with me to the grave, but…"
If I were asked if I had a thing for braided girls with glasses, I'd probably respond with some vague answer like, "Not really" after giving it some thought.
But as cliche as it may sound, I find myself not altogether disliking the look of this particular braided and bespectacled girl before me.
"Since when?"
"I'd say around summer in second year? There was a second-hand music store around here, and Takeya often dragged me there…"
An unusual girl who works extremely hard at the shopping district near the station during the evenings.
And for someone like me who paid attention to small details, the beautiful face behind those glasses felt out of place, to say the least.
It was on a particular day, just as we'd passed by each other in the school hallways, that I suddenly realized who she was… I almost screamed at that moment.
After all, it was so shocking, unexpected, and absurd that I could barely help myself.
"You've known about me for so long, Kitahara-kun…"
"Well, if we're talking about you, every guy in school's known about you for the past two years. At the very least, ever since the first year's school festival… Oh…"
"Sorry."
It appears that talking about how she became famous thanks to the school festival in front of her is off-limits.
"Today's the first time anyone's managed to recognize me like this. Even though I've been here like this for a year now."
"Really? Maybe everyone noticed but just kept quiet about it?"
Or maybe people just weren't sure what would happen if they called out to her…
Still, Takeya has shown no signs of recognizing her no matter how many times he has passed her by. And Io, who's in her class, didn't even bat an eyelid earlier.
"Not at all. I'm sure you're the first, Kitahara-kun. I've always had an eye for people."
"I-Is that so…?"
Somehow, I don't really understand the nuance of what she's saying. Does she see me as someone annoyingly persistent?
"U-Umm, so you see…"
"My family…"
"Eh…?
The moment I try to get to the main topic…
"Isn't really all that rich to begin with."
"Uh…"
She beats me to the punch.
"There are families who donate a ridiculous amount of money. But still, our school's tuition fee is very high, even among private schools. When I enrolled, we were really pushing it."
Most likely, Ogiso is trying to share aspects of her life that she has never told anyone about before.
"Ogiso…"
This is bad… This isn't how I wanted this to play out.
"But I was able to have fun as usual when I enrolled. I'd be with people, stopping at places on the way home, going shopping, drinking tea and chatting, and going to karaoke."
If I hear any more about Ogiso's painful situation, I won't be able to accomplish my original goal.
"That life of mine changed about two years ago… During my first year in school, when fall was about to change into winter."
I'll no longer be able to just selfishly ask her to spend the whole month on this pet project of mine.
"Could it be that… something happened to your family?"
Even so, I must keep listening.
After all, Ogiso has resolved to talk about it with a nobody like me…
"No, it's something that happened to me."
Which is why I choose to forget about my insignificant plan, and ready myself to listen until the end…
"After I'd won Miss Houjou High, people started treating me like some sort of 'lady,' and things became quite troublesome…"
"…Huh?"
"Umm, well… I never really hated it, so I just laughed it off, but before long I couldn't even back out."
"…What?"
"When that happened, I had to do so many things just to preserve my image…"
"I couldn't take up people's invitations until I bought new clothes, and to do that, I had to take a part-time job without anyone knowing… …And because of that, I couldn't spend time with anyone."
"…I see…"
"Well, I thought that I was overthinking it. But then I'd hear rumors about myself every so often, like what clothes I wore somewhere, or what my hairstyle was that day…"
"…I've also heard plenty of those."
"Right? That's why I can't let people see me working at a grocery store in casual clothing."
"Even so, why are you working here, then? Instead of a place that provides you with a cute uniform."
"Because the store is run by one of my dad's acquaintances. He wouldn't let me work anywhere else."
"So, your dad's doing well…"
"So is my mom, you know?"
"That's good to hear…"
Indeed, that's good to hear in more ways than one…
Her parents are doing well, and she talks with her family about taking a part-time job.
On top of that, her father has found somewhere for her to work. It may be a rather plain job, but his daughter is working as hard as she can.
The image of a warm and loving family pops up in my head.
"It's difficult… The less I spend time with others, the more they talk about me like I'm nobility. I can't hang out with people casually anymore."
"Is that… so…"
"Yes…"
For that reason, I can't think of what to say to her now that she's finished.
To be honest, I'm stumped…
Having heard her somewhat lackluster confession, I'm on the fence about whether I should push onward or pull back.
What Ogiso confessed wasn't anything too burdening or trivial, and it wasn't like I didn't understand it either. But it just makes me wonder what the big deal was.
The fact that it's not a big deal makes it even harder to find the right decision. Will I push my wishes onto her, or will I take her situation into consideration…?
"Could I head home soon? I'm making dinner tonight."
Ogiso gives me a cheerful look, making me wonder whether she'd noticed I was hesitating just now.
"So you also make dinner…"
"My mom makes dinner three times a week. Also, my hungry younger brother is coming home soon."
"That's impressive."
"They let me have a say on my choice of university, and my part-time job, so it's only natural."
"I see…"
This is the true identity of the school's number one lady.
Perhaps she's the most average person at school. In a way, she's nothing more than a normal, good girl.
"And, umm… about today…"
"There's no way I'd tell anyone. I hope you can believe me."
Which is why it's becoming harder and harder for me to endure this.
"Thanks. I trust you."
"Don't place your trust in me so easily. You do know why I came here, right?"
"Why… you came…?"
You shouldn't easily believe in cool-headed people who take advantage of others' weaknesses, or selfish people who don't consider others' circumstances.
"…It's nothing. Yeah, I definitely won't tell. So…"
Tormented with regret for not asking her when I had her under my thumb, and the guilt of not being able to look at her radiant figure directly, I turn my back to Ogiso as if to flee from her.
The thing is, when I talk with Ogiso, it's as if I'm a selfish, trivial, and small-minded… no, she just made me realize that I really am that type of person.
"Kitahara-kun."
"Hmm?"
Even so, Ogiso keeps her innocent expression, and calls out to stop me.
"You know… I'd like to talk with you again tonight… would that be okay?"
"Tonight…?"
"I know, let's meet in front of Minami-Suetsugu Station at 10 o'clock. I'll be waiting."
Minami-Suetsugu is different from Suetsugu-chou, being a business district that doesn't sleep, even in the dead of night.
"10 o'clock… Ogiso?"
Asking me to come to such a place at that time is…
"Because you still have the wrong idea about me Kitahara-kun… no, perhaps it's just that I haven't told you the truth."
"The… wrong idea?"
"The real me, you see… isn't the good girl you currently have in mind."
Just the two of us, in the night of the business district…
And… the real Ogiso?
The time right now is 10:42 PM.
The location is the fifth floor of the Daimachi Building, three minutes from the Minami-Suetsugu Station by foot.
"Ha… haha…"
Karaoke House Mayflower, Room 15.
"Hahahahaha… ahahahahaha…"
"Fuaaaah… time for a break. Thank you for listening so attentively!"
"Aha, ahahaha, ahahahahahahaha!"
"Haah, I'm parched! Ah, excuse me. This is Room 15. I'd like some oolong tea and… Kitahara-kun, what'll you have?"
"I'm okay, I'm okay! I'm already stuffed!"
After having sung eight songs in a row, Ogiso finally takes a seat on the sofa… right beside me, as if it was the most natural thing in the world.
"Umm… since we went through the new songs for the time being, next will be the usual ones, right?"
"R-Right…"
This girl just directly inputs the code without using the table of contents or even the search function…
Moreover, despite having asked me, "What'll you drink?", she's never actually asked me, "What'll you sing?" even once.
The business district. The two of us alone, in the middle of the night.
And this is… the real Ogiso.
"Haha, hahaha…"
I knew it. I knew it'd be like this… not.
I figured there'd be some kind of punchline, but I never imagined this…
"…Did I disappoint you?"
"Not at all, really!"
This is badーI can't even lie anymore.
"This is my 'true self.' My very last secret."
The heater is on so high, and I can't stop sweating… Despite my face burning, only cold sweat drips down.
"Once a week I come here to sing karaoke by myself… Is it weird after all?"
"No, no, no, I understand! There are girls like that!"
She's the first girl I've ever met who's done this, though.
"R-Right! You're busy with work, so you can't really spend a lot of time together with friends!"
"Ah, no, that's not it. I just want to sing karaoke by myself."
"Eh… really?"
"Because if everyone was here, then the price per song would increase, right?"
"Per song…?"
"Besides, it's hard to get a turn if there are too many people, and it's irritating when I have to wait too long.
It's such a waste if you can't even get through ten songs in two hours, you know?"
"Irritating… a waste…"
"On that note, one person can sing 30 songs in two hours. And if you start singing right after the previous song ends, you can fit in about five more."
"Non-stop…"
"Besides, my friends I made in first year don't invite me anymore. When I was with everyone, I put in a request for five songs in a row, and it really annoyed them…"
"There are girls like that, yeah…"
They're mostly infamous for that, though.
"I'm sorry. But you see, when it comes to singing, I don't back down no matter what, nor do I think of others."
"Ah…"
"That's why, when I heard a song I'm good at… not to mention it being my favorite song, there was no way I could hold it in."
So that's… the reason.
"It was really fun. I was so happy. And… it felt really good too."
"Ogiso…"
After closing her eyes to remember that moment, Ogiso puts on a delighted, enchanting face.
"You see, Kitahara-kun… I did refuse you at first, right?"
The hesitation that I called "not wanting to sing in front of others" never existed to begin with.
"I was thinking about whether someone like me could do it, whether I could do it the way I am now, and whether I really wanted to do it."
"Y-Yeah… you did."
"I thought I couldn't do it. I thought I couldn't do it the way I am now."
"But, you know… I really wanted to give it a try."
It had nothing to do with her singing in front of people, or singing by herself.
"That's why, even though I'd refused for two out of the three reasons, ever since then, I'd been worrying about it, and regretting it."
Compared to the simple desire of "wanting to sing," the location, the audience, and the surroundings mean nothing to Ogiso.
"Hey, Kitahara-kun."
"…Hmm?"
"…Once again, I'm renouncing my withdrawal. I'm sorry for having you go round in circles like this."
"For my introduction… I'm Ogiso Setsuna, Class 3-A. My family consists of four people. My best subject is English, my worst… it's silly, but classical stuff."
Ogiso sticks out her tongue for an instant, taking the microphone and standing up, as if to cover up various important things about herself.
"My hobby is singing. I'm especially good at singing for a long time. I can sing without any problems for three hours, non-stop."
What starts playing in the background is that song. The song which served as our common language when we first met, as if to commemorate our meeting again.
"My motivation for going on stage at the school festival… Umm, whatever it may be, it's my first time, so I might end up holding everyone back."
The words coming from her mouth are the words I've wanted her to say all day today, but the ones I just couldn't get her to say.
"But even if I'm not good enough at the performance and it makes everyone laugh, I won't give up and will continue singing until the very end. Thank you!"
This isn't because my efforts paid off though. It's only because Ogiso is kind and she happens to really, really like singing.
Even so, I'm still delighted about tonight. To think that everything would turn out so well in the end.
"Hey, Kitahara-kun."
"Eh?"
"With this, Ogiso Setsuna's last secret has been revealed… You've just learned all about me."
The heater is on so high, I just can't stop sweating.
…Despite my face burning… I really am breaking out in a cold sweat.
